Page structure for restaurant details, menus, review forms, and branch screens.
HTML is the standard markup language used to structure web pages. In a
multi - restaurant food review system, HTML defines restaurant cards,
cuisine filters, branch details, menu tables, rating panels, review forms,
owner dashboards, and report sections. It creates the hierarchy needed for
clear discovery and structured feedback collection across the platform.
Page structure Review forms Accessible layout
HTML forms the base layer that lets users browse restaurants and submit
structured feedback through well - organized page sections.

Client - side logic for live filters, ratings, and review validation.
JavaScript adds interactivity and responsiveness to the review experience.
It can update restaurant filters, handle live search, capture star
ratings, validate review fields, preview uploaded images, and refresh
dashboard components without forcing full page reloads. This makes the
platform feel faster and more reliable while users explore or post

Visual styling for responsive, branded, and easy - to - compare interfaces.
CSS controls the presentation of web pages by styling colors, spacing,
typography, cards, buttons, filters, and responsive layouts. For a
restaurant review system, CSS helps create attractive restaurant listings,
rating badges, menu tabs, review cards, moderation states, and dashboard
panels that work smoothly across desktop and mobile devices. A good CSS
layer improves clarity and trust during restaurant comparison.
Responsive design Rating badges Visual hierarchy
CSS turns the structured HTML content into a polished interface that is easy
to scan, compare, and act on.

Backend processing and relational storage for restaurants, reviews, and branch activity.
PHP handles the server - side logic required for authentication, restaurant
retrieval, menu updates, review submission, moderation actions, and owner
responses. MySQL stores relational data such as users, restaurants, menus,
branches, reviews, ratings, and reports. Together they create a reliable
database - driven foundation for trusted feedback and restaurant performance
Server logic Relational storage Report generation
PHP and MySQL work together to keep the review workflow accurate, secure,
and traceable from discovery to moderation.
